ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The parent term's Chan use is verbal tangle; this orthographic form sharpens it to talk treated as idle or unnecessary.
EvidenceBody: An early record warns people not to gather and talk idle vine-tangle, adding that the old man may catch and examine them. Two later verses call the whole great treasury of teachings 'idle vine-tangle': one immediately adds that the seventeen hundred cases trip people to death. A separate verse says that a massive volume already carries idle vine-tangle and puns that there is no need to send more 'idle furnishings.' The Zen deviation is the extension of the corpus's vine-language from individual words to gathered discussion, large books, the canon, and the case collection. The texts make those appraisals; this entry does not generalize them to every written record.
